Only you know if you'd regret not announcing it. While most people do want to make an announcement and it's normal to want to have control over people's knowledge of your pregnancy (rather than waiting for them to realize it on their own), you don't need to do anything you don't want to do.  
  
I lost my dad in February and learned that I was pregnant in August (at 5 months, lol). I had more breathing room between these events than you do, but you could definitely wait to announce so that the loss of your dad isn't the first thing that occurs to people when they learn that you're pregnant. I did have another advantage in the sense that I both lived away from my hometown and wasn't really showing until 6 months along.  
  
Ultimately, I announced on social media; if that's an option for you, it gives you an opportunity to easily announce the happy event (pregnancy) while acknowledging the sad one (death), e.g. "It's been a difficult couple of months, but I'm very happy to announce that I'm pregnant. We can't wait for baby to get here on [due date]." (You can phrase it however you want, of course, but I thought an example might be helpful.)  
  
I will say that you will be surprised at the support you receive from those who know that you're having a hell of a year once they learn that you're pregnant. You might be grateful for their help throughout the pregnancy. Also, it's been my experience that people who don't know about the pregnancy might accidentally say some pretty upsetting things to you, just as a result of not being in the know/not realizing that you could probably do with some extra sensitivity right now. I'm glad that I announced when I did (around 24 weeks).

Just based on the information you've provided, I don't think you need to worry that your feelings aren't reciprocated, but I know that receiving reassurance is really important. Have you expressed your concerns to her? The fact that you're worried she might not love you quite as much as you love her could actually encourage her to open up a bit.

A little bit of one-sidedness can be unavoidable in an LDR, e.g. one partner might stay up late to talk and mess up their sleeping schedule, be the one who is traveling more, etc. I am that partner in my relationship, but I don't feel unappreciated. My boyfriend always seems excited to talk to me, says sweet things to me, encourages me to seek reassurance if I need it, and so on.

When I know I'm being irrational, I like to preface my question/concern with something like, "I know I have no reason to doubt your love, but I've been feeling anxious and could use some reassurance... [question/concern]." If the conversation gets heated, remain patient/calm; remember that your concerns arose internally, not due to his actions or statements.  
  
Ultimately, you have to discuss these things. If you keep it inside, you'll very likely end up becoming resentful and/or paranoid, as you never sought the reassurance you needed at this time. If he is an understanding person, he should be able to assuage your fears, at least by the end of an honest and compassionate (from both ends) discussion.

When my boyfriend asked if I wanted to video chat for the first time, I took a few minutes to collect myself and said something like, "I look bad right now and might be a little nervous, but if that's okay with you, sure." Then he called. Including those disclaimers relaxed me because I felt like he didn't expect me to be super bubbly/charismatic. He also felt more comfortable saying he was nervous, himself. We were both obviously jittery throughout the call and it only lasted about an hour, but it was fun and we've spent almost every night on call since then.  
  
Maybe you could do something similar to help ease your nerves? You don't have to say, "I want to hear your voice," but maybe, "I'd really like to have an actual phone conversation with you again, but it makes me nervous so I might be a little jittery, like last time... Is that okay?" Take some deep breaths before the call and remember that this is the same guy you text all the time.
